column2: brushing your teeth in the morning and at night
column3: brush twice a day, after breakfast and last thing before bed
column4: food and germs make plaque that causes holes in the teeth, and at night less spit protects them

column2: deciding how long to brush
column3: brush for about two minutes, using a timer or a song
column4: shorter brushing leaves plaque on many tooth surfaces

column2: putting toothpaste on the brush
column3: use a pea-sized blob of fluoride toothpaste
column4: fluoride makes teeth stronger, and more paste than that does not clean better

column2: finishing brushing and wanting to rinse with lots of water
column3: spit out the toothpaste but do not rinse your mouth with water straight away
column4: the fluoride left on the teeth keeps protecting them for longer

column2: brushing hard to make teeth really clean
column3: brush gently in small circles with a soft brush
column4: hard scrubbing hurts the gums and wears the teeth

column2: missing the back teeth
column3: brush the outside, the inside and the chewing tops of every tooth, back ones too
column4: holes often start in the back teeth where food gets stuck

column2: forgetting the tongue
column3: brush your tongue gently too
column4: germs on the tongue cause bad breath

column2: gums bleed a little when brushing
column3: keep brushing gently and tell a parent if it goes on
column4: bleeding gums usually mean plaque is there, and gentle brushing helps them heal

column2: the toothbrush bristles are bent and splayed
column3: ask for a new toothbrush, about every three months
column4: worn bristles do not clean well

column2: a brother asks to borrow your toothbrush
column3: never share a toothbrush
column4: toothbrushes carry germs and blood from one mouth to another

column2: swallowing toothpaste
column3: spit it out, do not eat it
column4: toothpaste is for cleaning, and too much fluoride swallowed is not good for the body

column2: wanting to brush right after drinking orange juice
column3: wait about an hour after acidic drinks before brushing
column4: acid softens tooth enamel for a while and brushing then can wear it away

column2: staying at a friend's house overnight
column3: pack your own toothbrush and toothpaste
column4: you still need to brush, and you should not use someone else's brush

column2: the toothbrush after brushing
column3: rinse it and stand it upright to dry in the air
column4: a wet brush shut away grows germs

column2: being too tired to brush at bedtime
column3: brush anyway, it only takes two minutes
column4: night is when teeth are most at risk of decay

column2: food stuck between the teeth
column3: use floss or an interdental brush to clean between the teeth once a day
column4: a toothbrush cannot reach between the teeth

column2: snapping the floss down hard
column3: slide it gently between the teeth and curve it around each tooth
column4: snapping hurts the gums

column2: using a fork or a pin to get food out of the teeth
column3: use floss, never sharp objects
column4: sharp things cut the gums and chip teeth

column2: eating sweets all day long
column3: keep sweets for mealtimes and not too often
column4: each sweet snack starts an acid attack on the teeth, and many snacks mean many attacks

column2: drinking fizzy drinks every day
column3: choose water or milk most of the time
column4: sugary and fizzy drinks cause tooth decay

column2: a baby tooth is wobbly
column3: let it come out by itself, wiggling it gently with clean fingers if you like
column4: baby teeth fall out naturally when grown-up teeth push up underneath

column2: a baby tooth falls out and the gap bleeds
column3: bite gently on a clean piece of gauze or tissue for a few minutes
column4: pressure stops the small bleeding

column2: a grown-up tooth is knocked out playing
column3: hold it by the white top, not the root, and get an adult to take you to a dentist straight away, keeping the tooth in milk
column4: a grown-up tooth can sometimes be saved if put back quickly

column2: a tooth hurts when eating cold or sweet things
column3: tell a parent so you can see a dentist
column4: pain can mean a hole in the tooth that needs fixing

column2: opening a packet with your teeth
column3: use scissors or ask for help
column4: teeth can chip or crack

column2: chewing pencils or ice
column3: do not chew hard things that are not food
column4: they can crack teeth

column2: playing a contact sport like rugby or hockey
column3: wear a mouthguard
column4: it protects the teeth from knocks

column2: the myth that swallowed chewing gum stays in your stomach for seven years
column3: it passes through the body in a few days, but do not swallow gum on purpose
column4: the gum is not digested but it moves through like other food

column2: bad breath in the morning
column3: brush teeth and tongue and drink water
column4: germs grow in the mouth overnight when there is less spit

column2: it is time for a check-up
column3: visit the dentist about every six months or as often as the dentist says
column4: the dentist finds small problems before they become big and painful

column2: feeling scared before the dentist
column3: tell the dentist you are nervous and ask what they will do
column4: dentists explain each step and can stop if you raise your hand

column2: the dentist says you need a filling
column3: let the dentist fix it
column4: a filling stops the hole from getting bigger and hurting more

column2: getting a numbing injection at the dentist
column3: expect your lip and cheek to feel fat and strange for a few hours, and do not bite or chew them
column4: you cannot feel pain there so you could hurt yourself without noticing

column2: the dentist offers sealants or fluoride varnish
column3: it is a quick painless coating on the teeth
column4: it helps protect the back teeth from decay

column2: wearing a brace
column3: brush very carefully around the wires and avoid sticky and hard food
column4: food stuck in a brace causes decay and hard food can break the wires

column2: coming back from the toilet
column3: wash your hands with soap and water every time
column4: germs from poo spread illnesses like tummy bugs

column2: about to eat or help cook
column3: wash your hands first
column4: dirty hands put germs on food

column2: how long to wash hands
column3: rub with soap for about 20 seconds, as long as singing Happy Birthday twice
column4: short washing does not remove enough germs

column2: which parts to wash
column3: rub palms, backs, between the fingers, thumbs, fingertips and wrists
column4: germs hide in the parts people forget

column2: drying your hands
column3: dry them well on a clean towel or a hand dryer
column4: wet hands spread germs more easily

column2: there is no soap or water on a trip
column3: use hand sanitiser and wash properly when you can
column4: sanitiser kills many germs but does not clean off dirt

column2: after stroking a pet or cleaning its cage
column3: wash your hands
column4: animals can carry germs that make people ill

column2: after playing outside in the mud or sandpit
column3: wash your hands before eating
column4: soil can contain germs and worm eggs

column2: after blowing your nose or coughing into your hands
column3: wash or sanitise your hands
column4: cold and flu germs spread from hands to things others touch

column2: after touching raw meat or eggs while cooking
column3: wash your hands at once
column4: raw meat can carry germs like salmonella

column2: the soap at school has run out
column3: tell a teacher
column4: everyone needs soap to wash properly

column2: biting your nails or sucking your fingers
column3: try to stop and keep hands away from your mouth
column4: it moves germs from your hands into your body

column2: how often to bathe or shower
column3: wash all over at least two or three times a week, and every day when sweaty
column4: it removes sweat, dirt and smell

column2: running the bath
column3: an adult checks the temperature, and you put cold water in first, then hot, and test with your elbow
column4: hot water can scald skin badly

column2: getting out of a shower or bath
column3: step out carefully onto a bath mat
column4: wet floors are slippery and falls in bathrooms are common

column2: washing behind the ears, under the arms, the feet and the private parts
column3: wash every part of the body with soap, and dry well between the toes
column4: these places get sweaty and smelly and can grow fungus

column2: after a swimming pool
column3: have a shower and wash off the chlorine
column4: chlorine dries out skin and hair

column2: after sport or a hot day
column3: have a wash or shower and put on clean clothes
column4: sweat on skin and clothes starts to smell

column2: a younger sibling alone in the bath
column3: never leave a small child alone in a bath, call an adult
column4: small children can drown in a few centimetres of water in seconds

column2: wanting to use a hair dryer in the bathroom
column3: never use electrical things near water
column4: water and electricity together can kill

column2: sharing a towel
column3: use your own towel
column4: towels can spread germs and skin infections

column2: putting on dirty clothes after a bath
column3: wear clean underwear and socks every day
column4: they hold sweat and germs

column2: wasting water by staying in the shower a long time
column3: keep showers short, around five minutes
column4: it saves water and energy

column2: washing your hair
column3: wash it with shampoo when it looks or feels greasy, often two or three times a week, and rinse well
column4: clean hair and scalp do not itch or smell

column2: tangled hair
column3: brush or comb it gently from the ends upwards
column4: pulling from the top hurts and breaks hair

column2: sharing combs, brushes and hats
column3: use your own
column4: head lice and scalp infections spread this way

column2: an itchy head and a note from school about head lice
column3: tell a parent so they can check with a fine-tooth comb and treat it
column4: lice spread quickly and are easy to treat, and they are not a sign of being dirty

column2: teasing a classmate who has head lice
column3: do not tease, anyone can get lice
column4: lice like clean hair as much as dirty hair, and teasing hurts

column2: cutting your own hair with scissors
column3: ask an adult or a hairdresser
column4: it often goes wrong and scissors near the eyes are dangerous

column2: long hair near machines, fire or in science class
column3: tie it back
column4: loose hair can catch in moving parts or a flame

column2: the myth that cutting hair makes it grow back thicker
column3: it does not change how hair grows
column4: the cut end only looks blunter

column2: long dirty fingernails
column3: keep nails short and clean, scrubbing under them
column4: dirt and germs collect under nails

column2: cutting nails
column3: use nail clippers, cut fingernails following the curve and toenails straight across, or ask an adult
column4: cutting toenails too short or curved can make them grow into the skin

column2: biting nails
column3: try to stop, for example by keeping them short
column4: it puts germs in the mouth and hurts the skin around the nails

column2: a hangnail
column3: clip it with clean clippers instead of pulling it
column4: pulling it tears the skin and can cause infection

column2: a sore red swollen toe beside the nail
column3: tell a parent
column4: it may be an ingrown toenail that needs treatment

column2: wax in the ears
column3: wash only the outside of the ear, never push cotton buds inside
column4: ears clean themselves and buds push wax deeper or hurt the eardrum

column2: putting a small toy or bead in your ear or nose
column3: never put things in ears or nose, and tell an adult at once if it happens
column4: it can get stuck and damage the ear or block breathing

column2: earache
column3: tell an adult
column4: it can be an infection that needs checking

column2: water stuck in the ear after swimming
column3: tilt your head to that side and let it drain, and dry the outside with a towel
column4: water left in the ear can cause swimmer's ear

column2: something in your eye
column3: do not rub, blink and rinse with clean water, and tell an adult
column4: rubbing can scratch the eye

column2: looking straight at the sun
column3: never look at the sun, even with sunglasses
column4: it can permanently damage your eyes

column2: playing with a laser pointer
column3: never point it at anyone's eyes
column4: lasers can damage sight

column2: red sticky itchy eyes
column3: tell a parent and do not share towels
column4: it may be conjunctivitis, which spreads easily

column2: the myth that reading in dim light ruins your eyes
column3: it only makes your eyes tired
column4: but good light makes reading more comfortable

column2: the myth that carrots give you night vision
column3: carrots are healthy for eyes but do not give super sight
column4: the story came from wartime propaganda

column2: splashing chemicals or doing experiments
column3: wear safety glasses when told to
column4: eyes can be hurt for life

column2: picking your nose
column3: use a tissue instead and wash your hands
column4: picking spreads germs and can cause nosebleeds

column2: a runny nose
column3: blow your nose gently into a tissue, one side at a time, and throw it in the bin
column4: it clears the nose and keeps germs off things

column2: needing the toilet in class
column3: ask the teacher politely to go
column4: holding it too long is uncomfortable and not good for the bladder

column2: wiping after using the toilet
column3: wipe from front to back, especially girls
column4: it stops germs from the bottom reaching where you wee

column2: finishing on the toilet
column3: flush, close the lid if there is one, and wash your hands
column4: it keeps the toilet clean and germs away

column2: missing the toilet or leaving it messy
column3: clean up or tell an adult
column4: the next person should find a clean toilet

column2: using too much toilet paper or flushing toys and wipes
column3: use only what you need and flush only paper
column4: other things block the pipes

column2: a public toilet
column3: go with an adult or a friend when you are younger, never with a stranger
column4: it keeps you safe

column2: not being able to poo for days and it hurts
column3: eat fruit, vegetables and whole grains, drink water and tell a parent
column4: constipation is common and these help

column2: an accident or wetting the bed
column3: tell a parent calmly, it happens to many children
column4: it is not your fault and there are ways to help

column2: seeing blood in your wee or poo
column3: tell a parent
column4: it needs checking by a doctor

column2: about to sneeze
column3: sneeze into a tissue or your elbow, not your hands
column4: sneezes spray germs a long way, and hands spread them on

column2: coughing near others
column3: cough into your elbow and turn away from people
column4: it protects others from your germs

column2: a used tissue
column3: put it in the bin straight away and wash your hands
column4: used tissues are full of germs

column2: someone sneezes
column3: you may say bless you, and the person says thank you
column4: it is a polite habit in English-speaking countries

column2: a cough that lasts for weeks or makes breathing hard
column3: tell a parent so a doctor can check
column4: it can be asthma or an infection needing treatment

column2: sharing a cup or bottle with a friend
column3: use your own cup or bottle
column4: colds, flu and cold sores spread through spit

column2: food that fell on the floor
column3: the five-second rule is a myth, germs get on at once
column4: dirty floors can carry germs

column2: a classmate is coughing and sneezing a lot
column3: keep a little distance and wash hands often
column4: it lowers your chance of catching it

column2: a vaccination at school or the doctor's
column3: have it, it is a quick sting
column4: vaccines protect you and others from serious diseases

column2: the myth that going out with wet hair gives you a cold
column3: colds come from viruses, not from wet hair
column4: but you may feel chilly and uncomfortable

column2: the myth that antibiotics cure colds
column3: antibiotics only work on bacteria, colds are viruses
column4: taking them when not needed makes them work less well later

column2: a cold winter morning
column3: wear layers, a warm coat, a hat, gloves and a scarf
column4: layers trap warm air and you can take one off if hot

column2: a rainy day
column3: wear a waterproof coat and boots
column4: being wet makes you cold quickly

column2: a hot sunny day
column3: wear light loose clothes, a hat and sunglasses
column4: they keep you cool and protect skin and eyes

column2: the weather forecast says it will change later
column3: take a jumper or a raincoat in your bag
column4: weather can change during the day, especially in the UK, Ireland and New Zealand

column2: wearing wet socks all day
column3: change into dry socks
column4: wet feet get cold, sore and can grow fungus

column2: snow and ice outside
column3: wear boots with good grip
column4: ice is slippery and you can fall

column2: wanting to wear flip-flops on a hike
column3: wear proper shoes that fit
column4: your feet need support and protection

column2: walking home in the dark in winter
column3: wear something bright or reflective
column4: drivers can see you more easily

column2: shoes that pinch
column3: tell a parent you need a bigger size
column4: children's feet grow fast and tight shoes hurt them

column2: putting clothes on inside out or in the wrong order
column3: underwear first, then clothes, then socks and shoes
column4: it is quicker and clothes fit right

column2: a school uniform that is dirty
column3: put it in the wash and wear a clean one
column4: clean clothes are healthier and others notice smell

column2: how much sleep a 9 or 10 year old needs
column3: about 9 to 12 hours each night
column4: the body grows and the brain stores what you learnt while you sleep

column2: wanting to stay up late on a school night
column3: go to bed at your usual time
column4: tired children find it hard to concentrate, learn and stay in a good mood

column2: using a tablet or phone in bed
column3: put screens away about an hour before sleep and keep them out of the bedroom
column4: the light and excitement make it harder to fall asleep

column2: not being able to fall asleep
column3: lie quietly, breathe slowly or read a calm book
column4: calm activities help the body relax

column2: a nightmare wakes you up
column3: remind yourself it was a dream and go to a parent if you are scared
column4: dreams cannot hurt you and talking helps

column2: a bedtime routine
column3: do the same things each night: bath, teeth, pyjamas, story, lights out
column4: a routine tells your body it is time to sleep

column2: a drink with caffeine like cola or energy drinks in the evening
column3: avoid them, especially before bed
column4: caffeine keeps you awake, and energy drinks are not for children

column2: sleeping in on weekends until noon
column3: keep wake-up times fairly similar each day
column4: a steady rhythm makes it easier to get up on Monday

column2: a messy, hot or noisy bedroom
column3: keep it dark, quiet and cool
column4: good conditions help deep sleep

column2: sleepwalking or talking in sleep
column3: it is common in children and usually harmless, tell a parent
column4: they can keep you safe at night

column2: breakfast before school
column3: eat breakfast every morning
column4: it gives you energy to think and play until lunch

column2: a plate at dinner
column3: try to fill half with vegetables and fruit, a quarter with grains like bread or rice, a quarter with protein like meat, fish, beans or eggs
column4: different foods give the body different things it needs

column2: not wanting to try a new vegetable
column3: try a small bite, maybe several times
column4: tastes change and many foods you dislike at first become liked

column2: eating very fast
column3: chew well and eat slowly
column4: it helps digestion and you notice when you are full

column2: eating while running or lying down
column3: sit down to eat
column4: you can choke if you run or lie while eating

column2: being full but there is food left
column3: it is all right to stop when full, say politely that you have had enough
column4: listening to your body keeps it healthy

column2: crisps and sweets instead of lunch
column3: keep treats small and occasional
column4: they have little goodness and lots of salt, sugar and fat

column2: fruit from the shop
column3: wash fruit and vegetables before eating
column4: they may have dirt or chemicals on them

column2: food past its use-by date or smelling bad
column3: do not eat it and tell an adult
column4: spoiled food can cause food poisoning

column2: food left out of the fridge on a hot day
column3: do not eat it if it has been out for hours
column4: germs grow fast in warm food

column2: eating raw cookie dough or uncooked meat
column3: wait for it to be cooked properly
column4: raw eggs, flour and meat can carry germs

column2: a friend at school offers you part of their lunch
column3: you may share only if neither of you has allergies and adults agree
column4: some foods are dangerous for people with allergies

column2: someone says your body or food is disgusting
column3: do not comment on other people's bodies or food
column4: it hurts feelings and every family eats differently

column2: being hungry between meals
column3: have a healthy snack like fruit, yoghurt or nuts if not allergic
column4: it keeps energy steady

column2: choking on food
column3: a coughing person should keep coughing, and if they cannot breathe or speak, shout for an adult and call the emergency number
column4: an adult can give back blows and abdominal thrusts

column2: whole grapes and hard sweets for little brothers and sisters
column3: cut grapes lengthways for small children
column4: small round food can block a small child's airway

column2: the myth that you must wait an hour after eating before swimming
column3: you can swim after a normal meal, perhaps waiting a little after a huge one
column4: there is no good evidence it causes drowning

column2: being thirsty
column3: drink water, about six to eight cups a day, more when hot or active
column4: your body needs water to work well

column2: a long sports session
column3: take a water bottle and drink often
column4: you lose water by sweating

column2: sugary juice with every meal
column3: drink water or milk, juice only once a day and small
column4: juice has lots of sugar

column2: drinking water from a river or stream on a walk
column3: do not drink it unless an adult says it is safe
column4: it may contain germs

column2: adults' drinks like alcohol, coffee or energy drinks
column3: they are not for children
column4: they can harm a growing body

column2: waking up with a fever and feeling hot
column3: tell a parent, rest and drink fluids
column4: rest helps the body fight the infection

column2: being sick or having diarrhoea
column3: stay home and keep sipping water, and in the UK stay off school until 48 hours after the last time
column4: tummy bugs spread very easily

column2: wanting to go to school with a high temperature
column3: stay home until you have had no fever for at least a day
column4: you could make others ill and you need rest

column2: feeling a bit ill but wanting to play outside
column3: rest quietly
column4: the body needs energy to fight illness

column2: a rash that does not fade when you press a glass on it
column3: tell an adult at once, it needs urgent medical help
column4: it can be a sign of a very serious infection like meningitis

column2: a sore throat
column3: drink warm or cool drinks, rest and tell a parent if it is very bad
column4: most get better by themselves in a few days

column2: chickenpox spots that itch
column3: try not to scratch, keep nails short and use cooling lotion an adult gives
column4: scratching can cause infection and scars

column2: the myth feed a cold, starve a fever
column3: eat what you can and drink plenty whether you have a cold or a fever
column4: the body needs fluids and energy in both

column2: visiting someone who is ill
column3: wash your hands and keep your distance if they are infectious
column4: it protects you and them

column2: a classmate is often away ill
column3: be kind and help them catch up
column4: being ill and missing school is hard

column2: a friend has a long-term illness like diabetes or epilepsy
column3: learn what to do and tell an adult if they seem unwell
column4: you can help keep them safe

column2: a friend has a seizure
column3: do not hold them down or put anything in their mouth, move hard things away and fetch an adult
column4: it protects them from injury while it passes

column2: a friend with diabetes looks shaky, pale and confused
column3: tell an adult at once, they may need sugar quickly
column4: their blood sugar may be too low

column2: finding pills on the table
column3: never take medicine unless a trusted adult gives it to you
column4: the wrong medicine or dose can poison you

column2: medicine that looks like sweets
column3: never eat it
column4: medicines are dangerous in the wrong amount

column2: a friend offers you their medicine
column3: never take someone else's medicine
column4: it was meant for their body and illness

column2: finishing a course of antibiotics
column3: take it all as the doctor says, even when you feel better
column4: stopping early can let the infection come back

column2: a grown-up thinks of giving aspirin for a headache
column3: aspirin should not be given to children under 16 unless a doctor says
column4: it can cause a rare but serious illness called Reye's syndrome

column2: swallowed something poisonous or medicine by mistake
column3: tell an adult immediately so they can call poison control or emergency help
column4: quick help can stop serious harm

column2: cleaning products under the sink
column3: never drink or play with them
column4: they are poisonous and can burn

column2: going for a check-up
column3: answer the doctor's questions honestly
column4: the doctor needs the truth to help you

column2: the doctor asks to look in your ears and throat
column3: let them, it does not hurt
column4: it shows them what is wrong

column2: being scared of a needle
column3: it is normal, look away and breathe slowly
column4: it is over in a second and protects you

column2: the doctor needs to look at a private part of your body
column3: a parent or carer should be in the room and the doctor explains why
column4: that keeps you safe and comfortable

column2: an emergency in the USA or Canada
column3: call 911
column4: it reaches police, fire and ambulance

column2: an emergency in the UK
column3: call 999, or 112 which also works
column4: it reaches police, fire and ambulance

column2: an emergency in Ireland
column3: call 112 or 999
column4: both reach the emergency services

column2: an emergency in Australia
column3: call 000, or 112 from a mobile
column4: it reaches police, fire and ambulance

column2: an emergency in New Zealand
column3: call 111
column4: it reaches police, fire and ambulance

column2: calling the emergency number
column3: say what happened, where you are, and stay on the line
column4: the operator sends help and tells you what to do

column2: wanting to call the emergency number as a joke
column3: never do it
column4: it can stop help reaching someone who really needs it

column2: needing medical advice that is not an emergency in the UK
column3: an adult can call NHS 111
column4: they tell you where to get the right help

column2: going to hospital
column3: ask questions and tell the nurses how you feel
column4: they are there to help you get better

column2: a small cut or scraped knee
column3: wash it with clean water, press with a clean cloth to stop bleeding, and cover with a plaster or bandage
column4: cleaning stops infection and covering keeps dirt out

column2: a deep cut that keeps bleeding
column3: press hard on it with a clean cloth and get an adult at once
column4: it may need stitches or a hospital

column2: a scab forms
column3: leave it alone, do not pick it
column4: it protects the new skin underneath and picking causes scars

column2: a cut becomes red, hot, swollen or has pus
column3: tell a parent
column4: it may be infected and need a doctor

column2: a cut from a rusty nail or an animal bite
column3: tell an adult
column4: you may need a tetanus injection or a check-up

column2: helping a friend who is bleeding
column3: get an adult and avoid touching their blood with bare hands
column4: blood can carry germs

column2: playing with knives or broken glass
column3: do not, and tell an adult about broken glass
column4: they cut deeply

column2: a bruise after bumping into something
column3: put a cold pack wrapped in a cloth on it for a few minutes
column4: cold reduces swelling and pain

column2: a bruise changes colour
column3: it goes from blue or purple to green and yellow as it heals
column4: the body is clearing away the blood under the skin

column2: putting ice straight on skin
column3: always wrap ice in a cloth
column4: ice on bare skin can damage it

column2: hitting your head hard in the playground
column3: tell an adult even if you feel fine
column4: a head injury needs watching

column2: after a head bump you feel sleepy, sick, dizzy or confused
column3: tell an adult straight away, you need a doctor
column4: these can be signs of concussion or something more serious

column2: riding a bike or scooter
column3: always wear a helmet that fits
column4: it protects your brain in a fall

column2: your nose starts to bleed
column3: sit down, lean forward and pinch the soft part of your nose for about 10 minutes, breathing through your mouth
column4: leaning forward stops blood going down the throat

column2: someone says to tip your head back
column3: do not tilt your head back
column4: blood runs down the throat and can make you sick

column2: a nosebleed that will not stop after 20 minutes or after a big knock
column3: get medical help
column4: it may need treatment

column2: after a nosebleed
column3: avoid blowing or picking your nose for a while
column4: the clot needs time to heal

column2: touching something hot like an oven or iron
column3: cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes and tell an adult
column4: cooling stops the burn going deeper

column2: someone says to put butter, toothpaste or ice on a burn
column3: do not, use cool running water

column2: a blister from a burn
column3: do not pop it
column4: it protects the skin underneath from infection

column2: a big burn or a burn on the face or hands
column3: get an adult to call for medical help
column4: serious burns need a doctor

column2: a hot drink on the table
column3: keep it away from the edge and from small children
column4: spilled hot drinks are a common cause of burns

column2: a splinter in your finger

column4: splinters left in can get infected

column2: a bee sting

column4: squeezing pushes more poison in

column2: a wasp flies near you
column3: stay calm and move slowly away
column4: swatting makes it more likely to sting

column2: swelling of face or lips or trouble breathing after a sting
column3: call the emergency number at once
column4: it can be a severe allergic reaction

column2: a tick on your skin after walking in long grass

column4: ticks can carry diseases like Lyme disease

column2: mosquito bites
column3: do not scratch, use a cool cloth or cream
column4: scratching makes them itch more and can cause infection

column2: being bitten by a spider in Australia
column3: tell an adult and keep still
column4: some Australian spiders are dangerous and need first aid

column2: touching stinging nettles

column4: the sting fades and rubbing spreads it

column2: a rash after touching a plant in the USA or Canada
column3: wash the skin with soap and water and tell an adult
column4: it may be poison ivy, which itches for days

column2: a dog bite
column3: wash it well and tell an adult
column4: animal bites often get infected

column2: a classmate has a peanut allergy

column4: even a tiny amount can make them very ill

column3: know where it is and tell an adult at once if needed
column4: it can save their life in a severe reaction

column2: you have an allergy yourself
column3: always tell adults at parties and friends' houses and read food labels
column4: they need to know to keep you safe

column2: hay fever in spring and summer

column4: pollen causes sneezing and itchy eyes

column3: never tease or try to trick someone with food they are allergic to
column4: it can be life-threatening

column2: asthma and a wheezy chest
column3: use your reliever inhaler as the doctor said and tell an adult
column4: asthma attacks can be serious

column4: quick help eases breathing

column2: going out in summer sun

column4: sunburn damages skin and raises the risk of skin cancer later

column2: swimming or sweating in the sun

column4: it washes and rubs off

column2: the Australian rule slip slop slap seek slide
column3: slip on a shirt, slop on sunscreen, slap on a hat, seek shade, slide on sunglasses
column4: Australia and New Zealand have very strong sun

column2: midday sun
column3: stay in the shade in the middle of the day
column4: the sun is strongest from about 11 to 3

column2: a cloudy summer day
column3: still use sunscreen
column4: UV rays pass through clouds

column2: getting sunburnt
column3: get out of the sun, cool the skin with a cool shower, drink water and tell an adult
column4: burnt skin needs care and shows you had too much sun

column2: a headache, dizziness and feeling sick on a very hot day
column3: move to shade, drink water and tell an adult
column4: it may be heat exhaustion

column2: someone in the heat is confused, very hot and stops sweating
column3: call the emergency number
column4: heatstroke is an emergency

column2: a dog or child left in a hot car
column3: tell an adult at once
column4: cars heat up very quickly and can kill

column2: a heatwave
column3: drink often, wear light clothes and stay cool indoors at the hottest time
column4: heat makes the body lose water fast

column2: fingers and toes going numb and white in snow

column4: it can be frostnip or frostbite

column2: warming frozen fingers on a radiator or fire

column4: numb skin burns easily

column3: go inside, take off wet clothes and get warm
column4: it can be the start of hypothermia

column2: licking a frozen metal pole
column3: never do it
column4: your tongue sticks to it and tears

column2: lips and skin cracked from cold wind
column3: use lip balm and moisturiser
column4: it protects dry skin

column2: walking on a frozen pond
column3: stay off ice unless an adult says it is safe
column4: thin ice can break and the water is deadly cold

column2: your body starts changing around 8 to 14
column3: it is called puberty, and it happens at different times for everyone
column4: hormones turn a child's body into an adult's step by step

column2: starting to smell sweaty under the arms
column3: wash every day and use deodorant
column4: sweat glands become more active during puberty

column2: spots on the face
column3: wash your face gently twice a day and do not squeeze them
column4: squeezing can cause scars and infection

column2: worrying that you are shorter or taller than friends
column3: everyone grows at their own pace
column4: growth spurts come at different ages

column2: girls starting periods
column3: it is a normal part of growing up, talk to a parent, school nurse or doctor
column4: knowing what to expect helps you feel ready

column2: boys' voices cracking
column3: it is normal as the voice deepens
column4: the voice box grows during puberty

column2: having questions about your body
column3: ask a parent, teacher or doctor
column4: trusted adults give true answers

column2: someone touches your private parts or asks you to keep a secret about touching
column3: say no, get away and tell a trusted adult
column4: your body belongs to you and no one may do this

column2: someone shows you pictures that make you uncomfortable online
column3: close it and tell a trusted adult
column4: adults can help keep you safe

column2: teasing someone about their body
column3: never make fun of anyone's body
column4: it hurts deeply and every body is different

column2: the correct names of body parts
column3: learn the proper names
column4: it helps you talk to doctors and adults clearly

column2: wanting privacy in the bathroom
column3: it is fine to ask for privacy
column4: as you grow you need more privacy

column2: being told you need glasses
column3: wear them as the optician says
column4: they help you see clearly and learn better

column2: not being able to see the board at school
column3: tell a teacher and a parent
column4: you may need an eye test

column2: cleaning glasses

column4: rough cloth scratches lenses

column2: taking glasses off
column3: use two hands and put them in a case
column4: that keeps them from bending or breaking

column2: someone calls you names for wearing glasses
column3: tell an adult and know glasses are normal
column4: many people wear glasses

column2: screen time making eyes tired
column3: follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds
column4: it rests your eyes

column2: playing outside
column3: spend time outside every day
column4: daylight helps healthy eyes and may slow short-sightedness

column2: listening to music with headphones
column3: keep the volume low and take breaks
column4: loud sound can damage hearing forever

column2: very loud noise like fireworks or concerts
column3: wear ear protection
column4: loud noise damages inner ear

column2: a classmate who is deaf or hard of hearing
column3: face them, speak clearly and do not shout
column4: it helps them lip-read and understand

column2: someone has a hearing aid
column3: respect it and do not touch it
column4: it helps them hear

column2: ringing in the ears after loud noise
column3: tell an adult and rest your ears
column4: it is a warning of damage

column2: finding it hard to hear the teacher
column3: tell a parent
column4: you may need a hearing test

column2: how much to move each day
column3: be active for at least an hour a day
column4: exercise keeps the heart, muscles and mind strong

column2: sitting a long time
column3: get up and move often
column4: it helps body and focus

column2: carrying a heavy school bag
column3: use both straps and pack only what you need
column4: it protects your back

column2: warming up before sport
column3: warm up and stretch gently
column4: it helps prevent injury

column4: it passes with rest

column2: feeling pain during sport
column3: stop and tell an adult
column4: playing through pain can make an injury worse

column2: a sprained ankle
column3: rest it, put a cold pack on, raise it and tell an adult
column4: it reduces swelling

column2: the myth that cracking knuckles causes arthritis
column3: studies have found no link
column4: but it can annoy people nearby

column2: feeling stressed or worried
column3: talk to someone you trust, breathe slowly and get some exercise
column4: feelings affect the body and talking helps

column2: a tummy ache before a test
column3: it may be nerves, breathe slowly
column4: worry can cause tummy aches

column2: feeling sad for a long time
column3: tell a parent, teacher or school counsellor
column4: help can make things better

column2: someone is unkind about how you look
column3: remember your worth is not your looks and tell an adult if it keeps happening
column4: everybody looks different
